extracted.intended_audience: readers and scholars interested in the history of secret societies, Illuminati, and Freemasonry
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of procedural rules, obligations, aims, and methods described for the Illuminati 'Scotch Knight' and related degrees — including ritual steps, selection criteria, strategies of influence, and oaths. Focused historical-analytical treatment of eighteenth-century secret-society practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chief study of the Scotch Knight
rubrics_metrics.description: "the chief study of the Scotch Knight is to work on all men in such a way as is most insinuating."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes subtle, insinuating influence on people rather than overt coercion; frames the central behavioral norm for members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to acquire property
rubrics_metrics.description: "He must endeavour to acquire the possession of considerable property."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material resources are an explicit expectation for the member — property as means to influence and support the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy and getting the upper hand in lodges
rubrics_metrics.description: "In all Mason Lodges we must try secretly to get the upper hand."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Calls for covert infiltration and leadership of existing lodges rather than public formation; strategic concealment of true control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceal true aims from ordinary Masons
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Masons do not know what Free-Masonry is, their high objects, nor their highest Superiors, and should be directed by those who will lead them along the right road."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate withholding of high aims and hierarchies from lower-level members; hierarchical guidance without transparent disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of ensnaring questions in candidate preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: "In preparing a candidate for the degree of Scotch Knighthood, we must bring him into dilemmas by ensnaring questions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training technique: place candidates in dilemmas via crafted questions to test or shape their responses and loyalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control and diversion of Lodge funds
rubrics_metrics.description: "We must endeavour to get the disposal of the money of the Lodges of the Free Masons, or at least take care that it be applied to purposes favourable to our Order"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial strategy: secure management or influence over funds so monies support the Order's aims while avoiding detection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advance the plan of Eclectic Masonry
rubrics_metrics.description: "Above all, we must push forward with all our skill, the plan of Eclectic Masonry"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic objective: actively promote a specific ideological variant ('Eclectic Masonry') as a strategic priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bonded loyalty to regard Illuminati as Superiors
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidate bond: "to consider and treat the Illuminati as the Superiors of Free Masonry, and endeavour in all the Mason Lodges which he frequents, to have the Masonry of the Illuminated... introduced into the Lodge."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obligatory commitment to act as agent for the Illuminati within Freemasonry, promoting internal change and allegiance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath commitments on virtue, opposition to despotism, and duty to report
rubrics_metrics.description: Oath (Nº VII) commitments: "I will never more be a flatterer of the great... I will powerfully oppose superstition, slander, and despotism... I will never sacrifice the general good... I will boldly defend my brother against slander... and will faithfully report to my Superiors the progress I make therein."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies moral-political stance and reporting duties: opposition to superstition and despotism, mutual defense among members, prioritization of the general good, and accountability to superiors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ceremonial injunction to 'prove thyself equal to Kings'
rubrics_metrics.description: At dubbing: Preses says, "Now prove thyself, by thy ability, equal to Kings, and never from this time forward bow thy knee to one who is, like thyself but a man."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ceremonial reinforcement of member self-conception as equal to, and independent from, monarchical authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure and opening of the Love-Feast (Table Lodge) ritual
rubrics_metrics.description: Love-Feast steps: open a Table Lodge 'in virtue of the ancient Master-word'; a bye-table with a chalice, pot of wine, empty plate, plate of unleavened bread covered by green cloth; stroke of Scotch Master by Prefect and Senior Warden; Prefect lifts the cloth and leads a commemorative narrative about "J. of N." breaking and blessing bread; examine hearts; close Chapter; no priest present; Brother Servitor quits the Lodge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an explicit step-by-step ceremonial script and symbolic elements; also prescribes absence of clergy and servitors during the rite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of priest presence at Love-Feast
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is to be observed, that no priest of the Order must be present at this Love-Feast, and that even the Brother Servitor quits the Lodge."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ritual rule: exclude ordained clergy and servitors from specific ceremonies — likely to control interpretation and preserve secrecy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Instruction to study symbols and report discoveries to superiors
rubrics_metrics.description: "Examine, read, think on these symbols... Should you in any future period think that you have conceived a clearer notion of them... declare your discoveries to your Superiors; it is thus that you improve your mind... they expect this of you; _they_ know the true path--but will not point it out."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogical rule: encourage individual study and discovery while requiring reporting to superiors; superiors guide indirectly without explicit disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim to use 'pure Reason' and secret associations to restore liberty
rubrics_metrics.description: "To get out of this state, to be freed and born again, there is no other mean than the use of pure Reason... This can be done in no other way but by secret associations, which will by degrees, and in silence, possess themselves of the government of the States..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ideological rationale: illumination by reason + secret, gradual institutional capture as the method to effect political transformation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate questioning on methods of change (open vs secret vs force)
rubrics_metrics.description: Series of candidate questions probing whether states and religion fulfill mankind's ends, whether to begin change by open support, forcible revolution, or other ways, and whether Christianity hints at this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection and indoctrination tool: use philosophical and tactical questions to determine a candidate's judgment about methods (gradual secret influence vs open or violent revolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification for use of means used by the wicked if for good
rubrics_metrics.description: Question/answer theme: "How far is the position true, that all those means may be used for a good purpose which the wicked have employed for a bad?" with injunction to take counsel from worthy persons outside the society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical guideline permitting pragmatic use of morally suspect tactics if they serve the Order's ends, tempered by consultation with respected figures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization of extreme measures when treated as sovereign prerogative
rubrics_metrics.description: Report that 'the power of the Order was extended to the putting the individual to death; and the reason given was, that "this power was allowed to all Sovereignties, for the good of the State, and therefore belonged to the Order, which was to govern the world."'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit acceptance of extreme, potentially violent measures on grounds analogous to sovereign authority — an instruction with grave moral and legal implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquire direction of education, church, professorial chairs, and pulpit
rubrics_metrics.description: "N. B. We must acquire the direction of education--of church-management--of the professorial chair, and of the pulpit. We must bring our opinions into fashion by every art--spread them among the people by the help of young writers."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strategic priority to control institutions that form opinion: schools, churches, universities, and the clergy to propagate the Order's doctrines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence reviewers, journalists, and booksellers
rubrics_metrics.description: "We must take care that our writers be well puffed, and that the Reviewers do not depreciate them; therefore we must endeavour by every mean to gain over the Reviewers and Journalists; and we must also try to gain the booksellers..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media-management tactic: coopt or neutralize cultural gatekeepers to ensure favorable reception and distribution of allied writings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt outward copies to remove offensive content
rubrics_metrics.description: Practice: "In one of them all the most offensive things in respect of church and state were left out."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tactical moderation: produce softened public versions of materials where necessary to avoid scandal or suppression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection criteria for Regent degree
rubrics_metrics.description: "We must as much as possible select for this degree persons who are free, independent of all princes; particularly such as have frequently declared themselves discontented with the usual institutions..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target recruitment: prefer independents and outspoken critics of existing institutions for higher degrees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence through women as a primary method
rubrics_metrics.description: "There is no way of influencing men so powerfully as by means of the women. These should therefore be our chief study... and cause them to work for us with zeal, without knowing that they do so;"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit tactic: cultivate influence via women by appealing to emancipation and personal admiration to mobilize indirect support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Win common people through schools, show, condescension and toleration
rubrics_metrics.description: "We must win the common people in every corner. This will be obtained chiefly by means of the schools, and by open, hearty behaviour, show, condescension, popularity, and toleration of their prejudices, which we shall at leisure root out and dispel."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mass-mobilization strategy: initially accommodate prejudices and display warmth and popularity, then gradually reform beliefs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coopt or decry influential writers
rubrics_metrics.description: "If a writer publishes any thing that attracts notice, and is in itself just, but does not accord with our plan, we must endeavour to win him over, or decry him."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intellectual management: attempt to recruit prominent authors; if impossible, actively discredit them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use learned societies and reading clubs as cover and engine
rubrics_metrics.description: "None is fitter than the three lower degrees of Free Masonry... Next to this the form of a learned or literary society is best suited to our purpose... By establishing reading societies, and subscription libraries... we may turn the public mind which way we will."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational tactic: conceal the Order's work under familiar civic or scholarly forms which can both hide and advance influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target cultural and professional institutions (military academies, printing-houses, arts)
rubrics_metrics.description: "In like manner we must try to obtain an influence in the military academies... the printing-houses, booksellers shops, chapters... painting and engraving are highly worth our care."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diversified infiltration: prioritize institutions with broad cultural reach, including the arts and military education, and use visual propaganda (caricatures, prints).

rubrics_metrics.name: Place members in judicatories and state offices
rubrics_metrics.description: "Could our Prefect fill the judicatories of a state with our worthy members, he does all that man can do for the Order. It is better than to gain the Prince himself."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal/institutional penetration: placing members in courts and administrative positions to effect long-term influence over governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual aid and preferential treatment of members
rubrics_metrics.description: "The power of the Order must surely be turned to the advantage of its Members. All must be assisted. They must be preferred to all persons otherwise of equal merit... The unfortunate must be relieved by the funds of the Society."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Internal solidarity: institutionalized patronage, mutual support, and preference for members as an organizational norm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher-degree ideological teachings (Magus/Philosophus and Rex)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reported doctrines: Magus/Philosophus "the doctrines are the same with those of Spinoza, where all is material, God and the world are the same thing"; Rex teaches that "every peasant, citizen, and householder is a sovereign... nations must be brought back to that state... by force if not peaceably."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core advanced ideology: radical materialism and a vision of universal sovereignty of individuals; controversial endorsement of forcible measures if peaceful means fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral-only transmission of highest mysteries
rubrics_metrics.description: "The system of these has not been printed, and the degrees were conferred only by Spartacus himself... They were only read to the candidate, but no copy was taken."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security practice: keep highest teachings oral and personally conferred to reduce risk of exposure and ensure control over dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational principle: concealment and use of cover names
rubrics_metrics.description: "The great strength of our Order lies in its concealment; let it never appear in any place in its own name, but always covered by another name, and another occupation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core organizational rule: operate under cover organizations and disguises (e.g., Freemasonry, literary societies) to avoid scrutiny while pursuing aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shape public reputations by collecting and presenting anecdotes
rubrics_metrics.description: "We must assiduously collect anecdotes, and the honourable and mean actions, both of the least and the greatest; and when their names occur... let them ever be accompanied by these marks of their real worth."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reputational management: curate narratives and anecdotes to influence perceptions of public figures, used in meetings and circulated writings.
